newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela jail island suffers first car theft.
newsitem.headline: Mandela jail island suffers first car theft.

text.p: Car thieves have struck in one of South Africa's remotest, and until now safest, communities -- Robben Island, where President Nelson Mandela spent 18 years in prison.
Police said on Tuesday they were investigating the first ever case of car theft on the island, which is five miles off Cape Town and only reached by government-run ferry.
South Africa has one of the highest rates of car theft in the world -- with tens of thousands hijacked at gunpoint each year.
On January 1, the island jail, whose last prisoners left in December, was formally declared a museum of the anti-apartheid struggle.
The stolen car was recovered almost immediately its loss was noticed on Sunday morning but no arrests have been made.
Nature conservation officials as well as staff from the prisons service and the department of arts and culture live on the island.
